name: Minaean
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Ancient South Arabian, unvocalized epigraphic corpus (Arbach 1993 is lexicon); stress unrecoverable/undescribed.

sources.note: Lists only Stein 2011 (subclassification) and Arbach 1993; alternative names Madhabic, Minaic, Epigraphic South Arabian.

Says the phonology was essentially like the other Old South Arabian languages and notes the unexplained non-etymological h in nominal endings/pronouns/particles; contains no information on vowels, stress or accent. Cites Kogan & Korotayev 1997 and Nebes & Stein.

sources.citation: Nebes, Norbert & Peter Stein. 2008 [2004]. "Ancient South Arabian". In Roger D. Woodard (ed.), The Ancient Languages of Syria-Palestine and Arabia, 145-178. Cambridge: CUP (reprint of the 2004 Cambridge Encyclopedia of the World's Ancient Languages chapter).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 149-150, section 3.3 Vowels: practically nothing is known about the vocalization of the ASA texts; syllable quantity cannot be determined with certainty, 'nor are any broad conclusions possible concerning the accentual relationships of Ancient South Arabian' (covers Sabaic, Minaic, Qatabanic, Hadramitic together). No stress placement given.

sources.citation: Kogan, Leonid E. & Andrey V. Korotayev. 1997. "Sayhadic (Epigraphic South Arabian)". In Robert Hetzron (ed.), The Semitic Languages, 220-241. London: Routledge.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 223 (Vowels): 'Since the South Arabian system of writing is purely consonantal, we cannot draw any direct information about Sayhadic vowels.' p. 224: the Minaean 'parasitic' h in external-plural affixes and construct nouns — 'Though it remains uncertain under what conditions this appears, it is thought that it was caused by a peculiar character of the stress (possibly even pitch).' No placement of stress stated.

sources.citation: Hommel, Fritz. 1893. Süd-arabische Chrestomathie: Minäo-sabäische Grammatik, Bibliographie, minäische Inschriften nebst Glossar. München: Franz'sche Hofbuchhandlung.
